description:
A tiny neural network learns to tell two spirals apart, one small step at a time. That is the whole trick behind how AI models learn: measure how wrong it is, find which way is down, take one small step, and do it again.

ML, slowly is a five-part series of music videos for people who have never heard these words: one idea per video, slow enough to follow on the first watch. #1 is how a model learns. Next, #2: Tokens (why it never sees a letter).

Everything on screen is one real training run, recorded at every step: a network with 337 weights (2-16-16-1, tanh), 200 points in two spirals, plain gradient descent with a learning rate of 0.3. The loss starts at 0.696; at step 3,121 every point is on its own side. The same network with a step ten times as big (learning rate 3.0) bounces and never gets down: 61% right after 5,000 steps. The landscape is a real 2D slice of the 337-dimensional loss landscape (Li et al. 2018): the two directions the weights moved most, which hold 99.0% of the path.

{chapters}

Made with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5): the lyrics, the song (ACE-Step 1.5; the music and the voice are AI-generated), word alignment, the training run, every frame (three.js), the render. Renderer forked from mexicat's p(doom) video (MIT).
